title: La Peña Madridista de Ceuta responde a Mbappé, Vinícius y Konaté sobre las camisetas
content:
La Peña Madridista de Ceuta responde a Mbappé, Vinícius y Konaté: "No entendemos su actitud, solo se trataba de apoyar"
Basado en hechos observados y verificados directamente por nuestros periodistas o por fuentes informadas.
Elígenos como tu fuente preferida en Google.
La Peña Madridista de Ceuta ha trasladado una protesta oficial al Real Madrid por la decisión de los tres futbolistas en el partido contra el Elche.
Mbappé, Vinícius y Konaté decidieron no mostrar el mensaje de apoyo a Ceuta en el inicio del partido ante el Elche, algo que sigue dando que hablar. Este jueves, la Peña Madridista de Ceuta ha trasladado una protesta oficial al Real Madrid por la decisión de tres de sus jugadores al no mostrar el mensaje de apoyo a los ceutíes en las camisetas que lucieron los futbolistas en el encuentro liguero.
"No entendemos la actitud de los tres jugadores, ya que aquí no era ningún tema político ni nada por el estilo, sólo se trataba de apoyar a una ciudad que lo está pasando mal", declaró a EFE el presidente de la Peña Madridista de Ceuta, Miguel Ángel Montano.
El dirigente ceutí comentó que han enviado el escrito al departamento de Peñas del club merengue.
"No comulgamos con lo que han hecho estos jugadores y hemos trasladado que el detalle no nos ha gustado porque hubiese sido mejor que no se pusieran la camiseta ninguno antes de hacer lo que hicieron", dijo.
Miguel Ángel Montano entiende que los futbolistas son "libres de hacer lo que quieran" y que no sabe "si será por algún tema de patrocinadores o algo pero lo cierto es que fue un gesto que no tenía sentido".
Recordó que España ha vivido otras situaciones parecidas como la DANA, el apagón eléctrico o los accidentes de trenes en Adamuz (Córdoba) "y ahora le toca a Ceuta vivir esta situación y este gesto de Vinicius, Mbappé y Konaté ha sentado mal", recalcó.
¿Qué opinas de que Mbappé, Vinícius y Konaté no mostraran el mensaje de apoyo a Ceuta?
Esta encuesta no es científica y sólo refleja la opinión de aquellos lectores que han elegido participar. Los resultados no representan necesariamente la opinión de los internautas en general o de los lectores al completo.
Los seguidores del equipo madridista en Ceuta vieron el partido en la sede de la Peña: "En un momento, y éramos unas 40 personas, pasamos de la euforia a la tristeza al ver lo que hicieron los tres futbolistas porque un poco de publicidad a Ceuta es mucho para nosotros en estos instantes", señaló.
El dirigente ceutí espera que el Real Madrid responda al escrito "porque es un club señorial y seguro que darán sus explicaciones".
La Peña Madridista de Ceuta, que se fundó en 1987 y que cuenta con unos 130 socios a pesar de llegar a ser más de 300 hace unos años, ha dejado claro que mantendrá su "fidelidad" hacia el Real Madrid.
Mbappé, el único de los tres futbolistas citados que hasta ahora ha hecho alguna declaración al respecto, justificó este miércoles su postura al decir que quiso tener un recuerdo para "todos los inmigrantes que han perdido la vida y también están en condiciones duras".
"Quería tener un pensamiento para toda la gente que sufre porque al final soy humano y no quiero poner prioridad al sufrimiento. Soy un chico que quiere lo mejor para el mundo que tenemos. Quiero dar un mensaje de positividad y de paz y espero que se solucione rápido", afirmó en declaraciones al diario As.

title: Meet the beekeeper carrying on three generations of family tradition
content:
The Honey Festival celebrates Kalbajar’s long beekeeping tradition, bringing local producers together as they promote the region’s honey and explore opportunities to reach new audiences beyond Azerbaijan.
Beekeeping has been part of Sabir Mustafayev’s family for generations. With more than 40 years in the profession, he says the craft has changed significantly, with beekeepers adapting to new challenges including global warming. His family brought its farm to Kalbajar in 2021 and later opened a honey shop there, followed by a branch in Baku. The annual Honey Festival is putting Kalbajar’s beekeeping tradition in the spotlight, as producers look to bring the region’s honey to a global audience.

title: Efter skandalerna – Norge sluter upp bakom nya kungaparet
content:
– Haakon är solid, säger den pensionerade läkaren Hilde Østrem, utanför slottet i Oslo.
– Jag är inte så säker på resten av familjen. Men hon (drottning Mette-Marit) har varit svårt sjuk. Jag tror att hon växer in i rollen.
Østrems grannar, som promenerat med henne utefter huvudgatan Karl Johan, är av samma åsikt.
– Nu måste vi ge dem en ärlig chans. Det här med Epstein var inget man önskade men det är dags att gå vidare, säger kontoristen Hans Bjørner.
Samlande kraft?
Haakon VIII blev kung och hans hustru drottning i samma stund som kung Harald avled den 28 augusti.
Fadern var väldigt omtyckt, många norrmän framhåller att han var en inkluderande monark som klarade att samla folket. I synnerhet det tal Harald höll 2016 verkar ha gjort intryck: Då sade kungen att hans landsmän kan vara födda i Norge eller ha invandrat från andra länder, att norrmän tror på ”Gud, Allah, Alltet och ingenting” samt kan dras till personer av samma kön.
Runt slottet, i samband med kung Haralds begravning, uttryckte många förhoppningar om att sonen ärvt den enande förmågan.
Stora rubriker
Ur det perspektivet har senvinterns rapportering om de nära kontakter drottning Mette-Marit haft med den avlidne och dömde amerikanske sexförbrytaren Jeffrey Epstein varit besvärande.
I januari stod det klart att hennes namn förekommer runt tusen gånger i de så kallade Epsteindokumenten. Drottningen ska bland annat ha lånat den sexbrottsdömde finansmannens bostad i Florida samt svarat att ”Paris är bra för otrohet” när Epstein skrev att han var på jakt efter en fru.
Avslöjandet skapade rubriker världen över och ledde till en skriftlig ursäkt från den dåvarande kronprinsessan som ”djupt beklagade” sin vänskap med Epstein.
I mars lät kronprinsparet sig intervjuas om Epstein.
– Självklart önskar jag att jag aldrig hade träffat honom, sade Mette-Marit då och lade till att hon blev manipulerad av sexförbrytaren.
Hon sade också att hon bär på stora skuldkänslor för Epsteins offer.
Rättegång och sjukdom
En pressad Haakon betonade parallellt att han måste ta hand om sina närmaste.
Då hade den uppmärksammade rättegången mot Mette-Marits son, den så kallade ”bonusprinsen” Marius Borg Høiby, inletts. Han greps 2024 och i juni dömdes han till fyra års fängelse för bland annat våldtäkt och misshandel.
Lägg därtill att Mette-Marits lungfibros stadigt förvärrades samt att Haakons syster prinsessan Märtha Louise något år tidigare gift sig med den ifrågasatte, självutnämnde ”schamanen” Durek Verrett.
En skandaltid, konstaterade medier och historiker – något som också speglades i opinionsmätningar.
Vid månadsskiftet januari-februari hade förtroendet för det norska kungahuset fallit till rekordlåga 60 procent, enligt public service-bolaget NRK. Ett sänke i mätningen var just Mette-Marit, vars förtroende då hade halverats.
”Verkar trygg”
Men nu verkar vinden ha vänt. Efter Mette-Marits uppmärksammade lungtransplantation i juni och kung Haralds död i augusti har stödet för monarkin ökat igen. 72 procent vill behålla den, enligt NRK:s mätning efter dödsbudet.
– Det har varit fint att se kung Haakon de här dagarna, han verkar trygg, sade Oslobon Elise Løver till TT i samband med kung Haralds begravning.
Även drottning Mette-Marit, som i samband med sin svärfars död visade sig offentligt för första gången sedan transplantationen, blir alltmer populär. Nästan hälften av norrmännen, 47 procent, tycker nu att hon är lämpad för rollen som drottning, enligt en undersökning beställd av Aftenposten.
I en liknande undersökningen i februari ansåg endast var femte norrman att hon passade som drottning.
Surfing och tacos
Samtidigt som Haakon och Mette-Marit blev Norges nya kungapar blev också deras förstfödda dotter Ingrid Alexandra kronprinsessa.
Den surfälskande och tacotokiga 22-åringen flyttade i våras hem från sina studier i Australien för att vara nära familjen under sin mammas lungtransplantation. Ingrid Alexandra beskrivs i medier som en populär och energisk prinsessa som inte är rädd för att sticka ut. Hon har gjort militärtjänst i armén och röt i vintras till i sociala medier om vad hon kallade ”personangrepp” mot sin mor och halvbror.
”Det är viktigt att inte komma med påståenden man inte har grund för”, skrev hon på ett privat konto som enligt NRK har 800 följare.
”Nu är det nog”.
Efter farfar Haralds död har hon värdigt följt sin pappa genom ceremonierna. Likt sin far har kronprinsessan avgett ett löfte i stortinget att styra Norge i enlighet med dess grundlag och lagar.
Banade väg
Norges nya kungapar firade nyligen 25-årig bröllopsdag. De två träffades i slutet av 1990-talet, då Mette-Marit var ensamstående mamma till sin då tvåårige son och arbetade som servitris. Genom åren har hon studerat kemi, etik och utvecklingsarbete och 2012 tog hon en masterexamen i ledarskap, enligt det norska hovet.
Att en blivande kung kunde gifta sig med en ”kvinna av folket” hade kung Harald redan banat väg för. Han umgicks med Sonja Haraldsen i hemlighet i nio år innan bröllopet i Oslo domkyrka stod 1968. Fadern kung Olav uppges ha tvekat kring sonens äktenskap med en icke-kunglig men tvingades till slut kasta in handduken.
– Jag minns striderna när Sonja presenterades, vissa spådde att det skulle innebära slutet för monarkin. Men hon blev en väldigt bra drottning, säger Hilde Østrem.
– Kungahuset kommer nog att hålla framgent också.

title: B.C. judge rules Vancouver city candidates can use Chinese names on ballot
content:
B.C. judge rules Vancouver city candidates can use Chinese names on ballot
Judge Roger Cutler released his decision on Friday, but his written reason will come later
Seven Vancouver city candidates who included Chinese characters in their “usual” name can have them on the ballot for the municipal election, after the city lost a court challenge on Friday.
Judge Roger Cutler of the B.C. provincial court said each of the seven applicants would be allowed to use their usual names on the ballot for the Oct. 17 election and that he would issue his reasons for his decision at a later date.
Cutler said his decision should not be taken as a statement that the city’s application wasn’t appropriate, and his written reasons will provide guidance for future elections.
Lawyers for the city and for the candidates submitted arguments to Cutler on Wednesday and on Friday morning, and Cutler took five minutes after lunch to announce his decision.
The “usual names” in all seven cases included Chinese characters in addition to their “English” names, and the candidates argued the Vancouver Charter allowed that.
The city took the case to court, saying it wanted guidance on whether the Chinese character names were their “usual” names and whether they should be allowed on the ballots.
Cutler presided over the hearing by video from Duncan to eliminate any perception of bias from a Vancouver-based judge.
City lawyer Grant Murray told the court he would inform the chief election officer of the decision and that the decision had come in time for the lottery draw to determine the order of names on the ballots that was scheduled to be held at 5 p.m. Friday.
“I’m relieved by the decision,” Iona Bonamis, who’s running for city council under the OneCity party banner, said by phone.
She said hopefully it will mean candidates in future will be able to include the names they are known by in their community without having to go through a court battle.
A message left with the city for comment was not returned on Friday.
The city’s chief election officer, Jason Twa, had argued the seven Chinese character names were not part of their usual names.
In addition to Bonamis, whose name is 陶思穎 (To Sie Wing), the other candidates are current ABC councillor Lenny Zhou or 周楠 (Zhou Nan) and Christopher Lee, a OneCity school board candidate, whose Chinese name is pronounced Lee Kei Peng (李基鵬).
Others using Chinese character names are Yuk (Alfred) Chien (錢育廷), Yunzia (Chris) Qiu (仇云霞), Lorraine Lowe (刘黛明) and Shirley SiO (邵己凌). Lowe is running for city council, Qiu for park board and Chien and SiO for school board.
During his submissions, Murray had told court that all the candidates, with the exception of Bonamis, appeared to exclusively use their English names and not their Chinese names on social media.
And he said that it was “odd” that the candidates hadn’t included their “usual” Chinese names on their original filings but added them later, at the last minute.
Of the 123 candidates for council, park board and school board published on the City of Vancouver’s website, seven included a Chinese name.
The Charter is the unique provincial legislation that governs the City of Vancouver. According to the Charter, nomination papers must include the full name of the person nominated and “the usual name of the person nominated, if the full name of the person is different from the name the person usually uses.”
Bonamis said earlier if the court allowed her to use her name, it would send a message that Vancouver respects different cultures and that it’s a multicultural city.
Lee, 18, said it’s important for him to have the name on the ballot because “it’s a core part of my identity.”
“I’m a very proud Canadian. I’m also a very proud Chinese Canadian,” he said. “Canada is a multicultural place and we should respect that, the electoral office should respect that.”
“I don’t think it’s about having the Chinese name on the ballot to win votes, it’s about … our identity. It’s what the people in the Chinese community know us as.”
It’s a sign that we can “represent every single voice that Vancouver has,” he said.

title: Gobierno y oposición anuncian avance en libertad de expresión
content:
Las delegaciones del Gobierno interino y de la Asamblea Nacional electa en 2015 emitieron la noche de este viernes 18 de septiembre de 2026 un comunicado conjunto en materia de libertad de expresión, como parte de los avances alcanzados durante el segundo día de trabajo en plenaria del segundo ciclo de diálogo. El mensaje fue difundido simultáneamente por Dinorah Figuera, jefa de la delegación opositora, en su cuenta de X, y por Jorge Rodríguez, quien encabeza la representación del chavismo, a través de su cuenta de Telegram.
En el documento, las delegaciones saludaron "con satisfacción" la decisión reciente del Ejecutivo nacional de levantar las restricciones de ingreso a portales digitales, una medida que, según señalaron, "fortalece el acceso a la información" en el país.
Asimismo, informaron sobre la instalación de la Mesa Técnica para la Libertad de Expresión, Pluralidad del Pensamiento y Derecho a la Información, un espacio que dará inicio a un proceso de consulta, garantías y verificación de los avances en esta materia junto a los actores involucrados y la comunidad en general.
El comunicado también anunció la conformación de una comisión paritaria de seguimiento, encargada de velar por el cumplimiento continuo de los acuerdos y compromisos establecidos. Las delegaciones indicaron además que permanecerán en sesión permanente hasta el próximo miércoles 23 de septiembre.
"Seguiremos informando los acuerdos alcanzados, de forma oportuna, en los próximos días", añadió Figuera en su mensaje en X.
Este anuncio se produce en el marco del segundo ciclo de negociaciones respaldadas por Estados Unidos, que comenzó el jueves y que las delegaciones de Rodríguez y Figuera llevan adelante en el hotel Meliá Caracas.
En esta ronda se espera que ambas partes alcancen además acuerdos sobre garantías civiles y políticas y sobre la continuación del tema judicial abordado en el primer ciclo, celebrado entre el 6 y el 12 de agosto, que culminó con acuerdos para la renovación completa del Tribunal Supremo de Justicia (TSJ) y la recuperación de activos de la reserva internacional del país depositados en el Banco de Inglaterra.

title: How to get digital copies of your UAE government documents on your smartphone for free
content: Dubai: If you’re a Dubai resident, you know that paperless transactions and communications are the way to go. That’s why the emirate has made getting digital copies of all official documents a simple process.Here’s how you can get digital versions of all your government-issued documents, right from your smartphone.Why do I need digital copies of documents?The shift to digital document management, rather than reliance on physical hard copies, is inevitable in a visionary city like Dubai.The government of Dubai has been taking proactive steps to create a fully paperless government for years. Launched in 2018, the Dubai Paperless Strategy eliminated more than 336 million sheets of paper used for government transactions every year, saving time, resources and the environment.Digital Dubai, the government entity that’s tasked with digitalising all aspects of life in Dubai, is leading the emirate’s shift toward a fully integrated, smart government.In April this year, His Highness Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence of the UAE, and Chairman of The Executive Council of Dubai, directed all government entities in the emirate to integrate services for individuals and businesses into a unified digital ecosystem within one year, with Digital Dubai overseeing its implementation.As part of these initiatives, ensuring government-issued documents are available to all residents without the need for paper, is a key aspect of the city’s vision. What kind of documents can I request, as digital copies?According to Digital Dubai, your UAE PASS permits you access to a host of documents available in official digital formats. Here are just a few examples of documents you can own digitally:Emirates IDPassport for UAE citizensDriving licenceVehicle registration card (Mulkiya)Attested academic certificates and recordsPeople of determination card (Sanad)How do I request digital copies? You will require your UAE PASS, which is your national digital identity, to request a digital copy of a government-issued document. Follow these steps to make your request:Download the UAE PASS app through the Google Play Store or Apple App Store. Log in with your biometric information.At the bottom of the home screen, tap on ‘Documents’ in the menu bar. Tap on ‘Request a document’.You will now be able to view a list of all official documents that can be requested, such as driver’s licence or academic qualifications equivalency certificate. Find your required document and click ‘Request’.Your Emirates ID card information will be used to request the document. Select ‘Confirm request’. Wait for the process to complete.Once the process is complete, you will receive a notification via the app. Click on ‘View document’. You will be to see the digital version on your app.Click on the three dots beside the document to be able to view more details and access other facilities, such as saving the document as a PDF, seeing the date issued, and removing the document. Fee: The service is free of charge.

title: Buffalo Puppet Procession Traces Native History Through NYC’s Streets
content:
Buffalo Puppet Procession Traces Native History Through NYC’s Streets
“Return of the Buffalo: Tatanka Owe Akupi” pays homage to 38 Dakota men executed by President Abraham Lincoln in Mankato, Minnesota, in 1862.
A herd of 40 life-sized buffalo puppets migrated through Lower Manhattan today, September 18, plodding through Bowling Green, Federal Hall, the World Trade Center, Chinatown, and several other historical sites along their trail. On the second and final leg of its procession, Return of the Buffalo: Tatanka Owe Akupi (Lakota for "buffalo trail home") will also hit downtown Brooklyn tomorrow, September 19.
Theater writer and director Amir Nizar Zuabi created the project with descendants of the Lenape, the original Indigenous inhabitants of New York, and Lakota elders, whose deeply sacred relationship with the mammal dates back thousands of years.
“We just followed the elders’ lead in who they wanted involved, what they wanted to be said, really letting them shape the conceptual backbone of the work,” JJ Lind (Cherokee-Shawnee), the artistic director for the performance group Immediate Medium, told Hyperallergic.
“We’d bring community members in to provide feedback on the activities that happen along the route,” he added.
At nine historic sites throughout Manhattan, such as Broad Street Plaza and Zuccotti Park, concurrent performances from the Native dance troupes, gospel choirs, and Lenape youth created a lively backdrop. From the rampant slaughter of buffalo in the 19th century to the species' recovery led by Native activists and conservationists, the procession traces the buffalo’s complex history in the United States.

title: Where Can Russian Athletes Compete After the IOC’s Provisional Ban Lift?
content:
Russia’s return to international sports competition was already well underway long before the International Olympic Committee (IOC) provisionally lifted its ban on the Russian and Belarusian Olympic Committees this July.
The shift began in September 2025, when the International Paralympic Committee voted against maintaining its ban on Russian and Belarusian athletes, paving the way for them to compete at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Paralympic Games, where Russian competitors won eight gold medals.
By December, the IOC recommended that international federations lift their bans on Russian and Belarusian youth athletes.
However, some individual governing bodies acted even earlier. The International Judo Federation became the first to restore full participation rights to senior Russian athletes in November of last year. World Taekwondo followed this January by approving the full return of both junior and senior athletes from Russia and Belarus.
Since then, eight additional Olympic sports federations have restored full participation rights to Russian athletes and teams, allowing the use of the Russian flag, national anthem and team uniforms.
Below is a list compiled by The Moscow Times detailing where and how Russian athletes can currently compete on the international stage:
Federations that allow full senior and youth participation
Archery: On August 14, World Archery reinstated Russian athletes, allowing them to compete under their national flag and bringing their status in line with Belarusian athletes, who were reinstated in May.
Aquatics: The World Aquatics Bureau lifted its ban on senior Russian and Belarusian athletes on April 13, 2026, two months after it lifted its ban on Junior athletes.
In its statement, World Aquatics President Husain Al Musallam said, “Over the last three years, World Aquatics and the AQIU have successfully helped ensure that conflict can be kept outside the sporting competition venues. We are determined to ensure that pools and open water remain places where athletes from all nations can come together in peaceful competition.”
Boxing: On July 30, World Boxing announced that it was restoring full participation rights to all Russian athletes.
"The Executive Committee accepted that Russian athletes would now take part in World Boxing competitions like boxers from any other national federation. However, World Boxing will strictly monitor the behaviour of Russian delegations during events as well as compliance with anti-doping protocols," the statement read.
World Boxing previously lifted its restrictions on Belarusian athletes on May 12.
Equestrian: The International Equestrian Federation (FEI) will lift restrictions on Russian riders and officials starting Oct. 5 and once again allow international competitions to be held in Russia, the governing body has said.
FEI had already approved a return to competition for junior athletes from Russia and Belarus on May 19, 2026, but did not change its stance that senior athletes should compete with neutral status at that time.
Fencing: The International Fencing Federation (FIE) reinstated Russian and Belarusian athletes on June 2, 2026.
“The decision reflects the FIE’s commitment to the fundamental principles of the Olympic Charter, including non-discrimination, equal treatment and the universality of sport, as well as the objectives and principles set out in the FIE Statutes,” FIE’s statement read.
On July 28, Russian fencer Pavel Graudyn won gold in the Men's individual sabre at the World Fencing Championships in Hong Kong, marking Russia's first gold at a major championship since the International Fencing Federation lifted its restrictions.
Field Hockey: On Sept. 17, the Russian Field Hockey Federation announced that it had received a letter from the International Hockey Federation (FIH) lifting all restrictions against its athletes and national teams.
Gymnastics: The Executive Committee of World Gymnastics released a statement on May 18, 2026, that it had decided to lift all restrictions on Russian and Belarusian gymnasts.
On July 28, 2026, European Gymnastics voted to bring itself in line with World Gymnastics in allowing Russian and Belarusian athletes to compete with their national symbols.
Handball: On July 15, 2026, the International Handball Federation (IHF) lifted its ban on Russian and Belarusian teams and officials, citing the IOC’s recommendation.
“The IHF reiterates its longstanding commitment to the Ukraine Handball Federation and continues to stand in solidarity with Ukraine. It strongly condemns the ongoing war in Ukraine and its devastating consequences. It is the IHF’s sincere hope that the conflict will soon come to an end, paving the way for a return to peace, the restoration of normal sporting relations and the resumption of peaceful international cooperation,” the IHF statement said.
“At the same time, the IHF remains committed to safeguarding the values of sport, promoting dialogue within the international handball family, and ensuring that its decisions continue to reflect the recommendations of the IOC and the interests of the global handball community”
Judo: The International Judo Federation, calling sport the “last bridge for reconciliation and peace,” was the first to allow Russian and Belarusian senior athletes back, doing so on Nov. 27, 2025.
“Athletes have no responsibility for the decisions of governments or other national institutions, and it is our duty to protect the sport and our athletes,” the federation’s statement said.
“Sport must remain neutral, independent and free from political influence. Judo, rooted in the values of peace, unity and friendship, cannot allow itself to become a platform for geopolitical agendas. The decision to reinstate full national representation reflects the IJF’s confidence in its ethical safeguards, as well as in the strength and integrity of the sport,” it continued.
Modern Pentathlon: The International Union of Modern Pentathlon lifted its ban on Russian athletes on July 13, 2026, citing the IOC’s recommendation.
Taekwondo: The World Taekwondo Council allowed Russian and Belarusian athletes back into the fold on Jan. 31, 2026, at a meeting in the United Arab Emirates.
Triathlon: Mikhail Degtyarev, head of the Russian Olympic Committee and the Russian Minister of Sport, said on Aug. 21 that World Triathlon had granted Russian athletes full participation rights.
World Triathlon lifted its ban on Russian and Belarusian junior athletes in April 2026, while senior athletes continue to compete as neutral athletes.
"This was made possible by the restoration of the Russian Olympic Committee's status. Earlier in April, World Triathlon already admitted Russian junior and para-athletes," Degtyarev said.
Volleyball: The International Volleyball Federation (FIVB) announced on July 8, 2026, that Russian teams and athletes would be restored to the World Ranking with the same World Ranking points they had at the time of the initial ban.
“The FIVB remains deeply concerned about the ongoing war in Ukraine and strongly condemns all forms of violence. We continue to hope for a peaceful resolution as soon as possible and remain committed to supporting the Ukrainian volleyball community through the FIVB Volleyball Empowerment programme,” FIVB added.

title: Amplían fecha para pagar el aguinaldo en El Salvador, ¿qué debes saber?
content:
Amplían fecha para pagar el aguinaldo en El Salvador, ¿qué debes saber?
El pago del aguinaldo en El Salvador podrá realizarse desde el 1 de octubre hasta el 20 de diciembre, tras una reforma aprobada por la Asamblea Legislativa.
Los trabajadores podrán recibir el aguinaldo a partir del 1 de octubre de cada año. La Asamblea Legislativa aprobó por unanimidad una modificación al Código de Trabajo que extiende el período disponible para que los empleadores entreguen esta prestación.
Con la reforma, el plazo queda establecido entre el 1 de octubre y el 20 de diciembre. Hasta ahora, la fecha habilitada para comenzar a pagar el aguinaldo era el 20 de octubre, según la modificación aprobada el año anterior.
El cambio fue incorporado mediante reformas a los artículos 197, 200 y 202 del Código de Trabajo.
Empleadores podrán elegir la fecha dentro del nuevo período
La iniciativa fue presentada por el Gobierno a través del Ministerio de Trabajo y mantiene la facultad de cada empleador para decidir cuándo efectuará el pago, siempre que lo haga dentro del período autorizado.
La normativa establece además que el aguinaldo deberá entregarse en un solo desembolso y que, bajo ninguna circunstancia, podrá pagarse después del 20 de diciembre.
Durante la discusión legislativa, el diputado Caleb Navarro, de Nuevas Ideas, explicó el alcance de la modificación.
«La reforma al Código de Trabajo es para permitir el pago del aguinaldo desde el primero de octubre. Estableciéndose el 12 de diciembre como fecha de referencia para su cómputo proporcional», dijo Navarro.
El legislador también se refirió al margen adicional que tendrán los patronos para programar el desembolso.
«Estamos ampliando la ventana para que el empleador pueda organizarse, organizar sus finanzas», agregó Navarro.
Desde ARENA, la diputada Marcela Villatoro expresó el respaldo de su fracción a la medida.
«Como grupo parlamentario vamos a acompañar, creemos que algo muy positivo para los trabajadores. Esperamos que también lo administren con responsabilidad», dijo Villatoro.
Aguinaldo proporcional para quienes tienen menos de un año trabajado
La reforma al artículo 197 mantiene el derecho al aguinaldo proporcional para los trabajadores que al 12 de diciembre todavía no hayan completado un año de servicio con el mismo patrono.
En esos casos, el monto deberá calcularse de forma proporcional al tiempo laborado, tomando como referencia la cantidad que le habría correspondido al trabajador si hubiese cumplido un año de servicio en esa fecha.
La modificación al artículo 202 también contempla qué ocurre si la relación laboral termina antes del 12 de diciembre. Cuando el contrato finalice con responsabilidad para el patrono o el trabajador sea despedido sin una causa legal, deberá recibir la parte proporcional del aguinaldo correspondiente al período trabajado.
Cambios también alcanzan retenciones y pagos al sector público
Los cambios aprobados también alcanzan la retención del aguinaldo destinada al pago de pensiones alimenticias. La reforma al Decreto 140 de 1997 permite que, desde el 1 de octubre, se aplique la retención del 30 % correspondiente a este concepto.
Además, se extiende hasta el 20 de diciembre el período para que las instituciones responsables trasladen los fondos retenidos por pensión alimenticia.
Otra de las modificaciones recae sobre la Ley de Compensación Económica Adicional en Efectivo, que regula pagos dirigidos a empleados del Estado y miembros de la Fuerza Armada.
Según explicó el diputado de Nuevas Ideas, Caleb Navarro, el cambio permitirá que estas compensaciones puedan comenzar a pagarse desde el 1 de octubre.
Propuesta para modificar el cálculo no obtuvo respaldo
Durante la sesión también se planteó un cambio relacionado con la cantidad de días de salario utilizados para determinar el aguinaldo.
La diputada Claudia Ortiz, de Vamos, solicitó aumentar los días considerados para ese cálculo, pero la propuesta no recibió el respaldo necesario.
Por tanto, la modificación aprobada se concentra en adelantar la fecha desde la cual puede efectuarse el pago, sin incorporar el cambio solicitado sobre los días de salario.

title: How modern tech aids Philippines disaster preparedness
content:
How modern tech aids Philippines disaster preparedness
MANILA, Philippines — Modern technology is increasingly aiding disaster preparedness in the Philippines, with the Department of Science and Technology (DOST) advancing artificial intelligence (AI) and other technologies to help save lives even before disasters strike.
AI is powering the government’s central monitoring platform, the Handa Integrated Platform for Preparedness and Response, which was launched in March to provide information on disaster preparedness across different hazards.
“It’s like the ChatGPT of disaster preparedness,” Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) director Teresito Bacolcol said at the Cagayan Valley Regional Science, Technology and Innovation Week press conference.
“You can type in what the different active faults are in Region 2 or any part of the country, and it will provide you with answers,” he added.
Bacolcol said the Handa platform has “simplified the assessment of hazards.”
The public can access the platform at handa.georisk.gov.ph.
Anyone can submit an incident report, which will be verified by the Office of Civil Defense and local government units with accounts provided by PHIVOLCS.
AI is also being used to improve weather forecasting by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration.
“PAGASA’s data are so big, so we need to use AI to improve forecasts; our target is five days to 14 days,” DOST Secretary Renato Solidum Jr. said. “The computing time to process the data would be every three hours. We are experimenting with the use of AI to shorten it to 15 minutes so that the forecasts are more up-to-date.”
PAGASA recently released its National Hydro-Met Observing Network, or PANaHON app, which provides near-real-time information from weather stations across the country.
DOST has also turned over a unit of the Mobile Command and Control Vehicle (MoCCoV) to the Tuguegarao local government.
The MoCCoV is a mobile command center that can be set up in remote areas in just 20 minutes.
It has three air-conditioned rooms that can serve as a command room, conference room, rescue or medical triage room, kitchen or independent bathroom.
It is also equipped with solar panels and a backup generator that can run for up to 32 hours.
In a speech to policymakers and disaster responders, Solidum said DOST is committed to investing in scientific research, hazard monitoring, early warning systems, geospatial technologies, impact-based forecasting and AI to allow the public to act with greater knowledge and lead time.
“But our responsibility at the DOST goes beyond producing information,” Solidum said. “Science must enter the decisions that shape people’s lives … Science and the information it provides must guide policies and influence investment.”
“The public expects information to move and decisions to be made. They expect resources to reach the people who need them. And they expect us to be ready before the emergency begins; that’s why convergence should produce a connected and operationally ready disaster risk reduction and management system,” he added.

title: Nueva York amplía la regulación para desarrolladores de Inteligencia Artificial
content:
Nueva York exigirá por ley que, a partir de noviembre, los desarrolladores de inteligencia artificial (IA) de vanguardia se registren ante el Estado y cumplan con estrictos estándares "de transparencia, seguridad e informes de incidentes", anunció este lunes la gobernadora Kathy Hochul.
La nueva regulación, en cumplimiento con la Ley de Seguridad y Educación en IA Responsable (Ley RAISE, por sus siglas en inglés), aprobada el año pasado por la legislatura estatal, exigirá que, a partir de enero, informen sobre incidentes críticos de seguridad en un plazo de 72 horas y proporcionen informes periódicos a la nueva Oficina de Innovación Digital, Gobernanza, Integridad y Confianza (DIGIT) del Estado.
Las empresas que no cumplan con las normas se enfrentarán a sanciones civiles.
Hochul anunció además el nombramiento del abogado Marc Gilman como director adjunto de la nueva Oficina de Innovación Digital, creada el pasado diciembre, de quien dijo que aporta años de experiencia en gestión de riesgos tecnológicos y cumplimiento normativo.
"A medida que esta tecnología evoluciona, utilizaremos todas las herramientas disponibles a nivel estatal para proteger a los neoyorquinos. Analizaremos detenidamente otras maneras de ampliar la Ley RAISE y fortalecer nuestras leyes sobre IA", indicó Hochul.

Incluso, dijo que no descarta explorar medidas de seguridad "como los interruptores de apagado automático de la IA si se consideran viables y beneficiosas para nuestro estado", algo que también evalúa California.
"En contraste con lo que acabo de decir sobre la importancia de actuar con urgencia, mañana Donald Trump se dirigirá a los líderes mundiales en la Asamblea General de la ONU. Recurrirá a sus tácticas habituales. Insultará a nuestros aliados. Incluso podría amenazar con anexar otra nación soberana. Pero lo que no escucharán es un plan serio y bien pensado para regular la inteligencia artificial", afirmó la demócrata.
Trump ha rechazado poner freno al desarrollo de la IA, como han sugerido los líderes del sector tecnológico, y, al contrario, ha dicho que creará la Fuerza IA y designará a un zar. De acuerdo con el mandatario, con las leyes existentes puede vigilarse esta tecnología sin necesidad de ralentizar su desarrollo y mantener la supremacía de EE.UU. en IA sobre China.
"Negarse a cumplir con sus responsabilidades, negarse a tomar en serio la regulación de la IA -quizás debido a sus inversiones personales en empresas de IA- constituye una abdicación de responsabilidad de proporciones épicas", aseguró Hochul.

La gobernadora hizo un llamado a la Administración Trump y a los líderes mundiales "para que den un paso al frente y se unan a nosotros, porque no puede ser solo Nueva York. No puede ser solo California. No pueden ser solo un puñado de gobernadores. Necesitamos una estrategia nacional y global".
El pasado viernes, el gobernador de California, Gavin Newsom, firmó una orden ejecutiva que endurece la vigilancia sobre las empresas de IA de ese estado y ordenó a su equipo evaluar la creación de un 'interruptor de apagado' obligatorio para los modelos de IA más avanzados, así como la instalación permanente de auditores independientes dentro de los laboratorios de las principales empresas del sector.

Calendario Anses: qué prestaciones sociales se cobran en la semana del 21 al 25 de septiembre
El organismo previsional sigue con la entrega de las jubilaciones, AUH, Asignaciones por Embarazo, entre otras prestaciones

La Anses (Administración Nacional de Seguridad Social) continúa esta semana con el pago de las prestaciones sociales correspondientes a la semana del 21 al 25 de septiembre, según está establecido en el calendario de pagos.

Cómo saber si tengo que cobrar alguna prestación de la Anses
Las personas que reciben prestaciones sociales a través de la Anses pueden consultar dónde y cuándo tienen el próximo cobro, el cual está determinado por el calendario de pagos que se realiza cada mes.
Para eso, deben seguir los siguientes pasos:
- Ingresar a la página de la Anses
- Completar el formulario con el número de beneficio o de CUIL
- Hacer clic en el botón “Consulta”
- Si corresponde, el sistema informará el lugar y la fecha de cobro (desde el primer día hasta el último en que se puede cobrar la asistencia en cuestión)
Cómo elegir el medio de pago para las prestaciones de la Anses
- Ingresar a Mi Anses o descargar la aplicación, con CUIL y Clave de la Seguridad Social.
- Seleccionar la opción Cobros
- Luego hacer click en la opción Cambiar medio de cobro jubilaciones y pensiones o Cambiar medio de cobro Asignaciones Familiares, según corresponda.
- Corroborar que los datos de contacto (correo electrónico, celular y domicilio) estén actualizados y verificados, lo que puede realizarse en el momento.
- Cargar el código de validación recibido por correo electrónico o SMS y confirmar el DNI, ingresando el correspondiente número de trámite.
- Una vez ingresado dicho código, se podrá optar por el nuevo medio de cobro dentro de las opciones habilitadas.
- En el caso de las asignaciones, podrán consultar el medio de cobro actual y seleccionar el nuevo.
Cabe destacar que quienes residan en zona austral deben optar por una sucursal bancaria para poder mantener el adicional correspondiente a dicha zona.
Para todos los casos, la elección estará vigente a partir de los 60 días de solicitada.

title: House passes act to make AI data centers pay for grid upgrades to minimize impact on residents — measure directs states to consider adoption of federal standard within two years of passing

House passes act to make AI data centers pay for grid upgrades to minimize impact on residents — measure directs states to consider adoption of federal standard within two years of passing
This rule could codify the promises that AI hyperscalers made to President Trump.
The U.S. House of Representatives just passed a bill that creates a federal standard requiring data centers to pay for grid upgrades made in their favor. H.R. 9340, also known as the Ratepayer Protection Act, amends the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978, which would require each State regulatory authority and each non-regulated electric utility to consider the adoption of the bill within two years of its passing, if it is signed into law.

This bill would ensure that data centers with a capacity of 100 megawatts or more would have to pay “the full, incremental cost of any generation, transmission, or distribution upgrade necessary to serve the load of such large-load customer, including in the event of such large-load customer terminating a contract or other agreement with the electric utility pertaining to the sale of electric energy, or otherwise ceasing the purchase of electric energy from the electric utility.” This bill closely follows President Donald Trump’s “Ratepayer Protection Pledge,” where he made AI hyperscalers, utility providers, and state governors promise that they will pay their own way when it comes to their electricity demands. All this stemmed from the surprise price hikes that many residential users and small businesses suffered from because of the massive demand by AI data centers and has become one of the primary reasons why the majority of Americans now oppose data center developments in their communities.
Oregon is actually one of the first states to have taken concrete steps in controlling the utility price increases when it passed the POWER Act in 2025. This law is even more stringent, with any development using more than 20 megawatts required to pay its fair share, and has already resulted in a 30% hike for data center electricity bills and a 1.3% reduction for residential power costs. Virginia has also followed suit soon after its governor signed the Ratepayer Protection Pledge in July 2026, with Virginia’s State Corporation Commission requiring data centers to pay for all required transmission infrastructure.
Even though the House of Representatives has already passed H.R. 9340, it still needs to go through the Senate before finally heading towards the White House for signing by the President. But even if it passes through the remaining hurdles, and the U.S. adopts a federal standard where large data centers pay for grid upgrades done in their name, it’s still up to each state regulator if they will adopt the standard. Furthermore, states have up to two years to make a final decision, meaning there’s a chance that the various temporary data center bans and moratoriums would have expired even before state regulators would have enacted this bill.

title: Congo rolls out Canadian-developed vaccine to fight Ebola outbreak
content:
Congolese authorities have begun rolling out a Canadian-developed vaccine in an attempt to protect 20,000 health workers from a fast-spreading Ebola outbreak, but Ottawa could be doing more to develop vaccines that are effective against the current species of the virus, experts say.
The vaccine, known as Ervebo and manufactured by Merck, was developed at the National Microbiology Laboratory in Winnipeg and has been deployed in outbreaks of the most common Ebola species, known as the Zaire virus. Its protective value against the Bundibugyo Ebola virus – the cause of the latest outbreak − is unknown, but health authorities have decided to try it anyway in a large-scale study.
Ervebo was developed and licensed solely for the Zaire virus, but it is the only Ebola vaccine available in large quantities today. There are no proven vaccines for Bundibugyo.
A leading Canadian vaccine researcher suggested in 2014 that the basic platform of what became Ervebo could be developed to target the Bundibugyo Ebola virus, documents show. The work was never done, and the international focus today has shifted to potential vaccines from other developers.
Ottawa temporarily bars entry for foreigners who visited Congo due to Ebola risk
The current Ebola outbreak has infected more than 7,670 people and killed nearly 3,700 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, according to official data Monday. It is already the worst Ebola epidemic in Congo’s history and is spreading faster than the world’s biggest outbreak, which killed more than 11,300 people in Liberia, Guinea and Sierra Leone from 2014 to 2016.
The outbreak has been fuelled by armed conflicts in eastern Congo that have destabilized the region and forced thousands of people to flee their homes. The lack of a proven vaccine has hampered the response to the crisis.
The vaccination campaign, launched Saturday, will target 20,000 front-line health workers in the epicentre of the outbreak, Congo’s Ituri and North Kivu provinces, over the next nine to 12 months to see whether Ervebo is effective against the Bundibugyo Ebola virus.
“Preliminary data suggest that it may offer some degree of protection against the virus,” said Guyguy Manangama, an epidemiologist and deputy director of Congo Ebola operations with Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF).
“In a race against time … we must use every tool available to us,” he said in a statement. “Even partial protection could help reduce severe illness and death. However, these potential benefits must be demonstrated scientifically.”
Ebola outbreak is outpacing response efforts, WHO chief says
Judie Alimonti, a scientist at the Winnipeg lab who helped develop Ervebo, wrote in a 2014 internal report that she strongly recommended the use of the same vaccine platform to create vaccines for the Bundibugyo and other Ebola viruses. But she noted that there was a lack of money to support the research work in Canada.
“The scientists would have happily continued working on it,” said Matthew Herder, a professor and associate director of the Health Justice Institute at Dalhousie University in Halifax.
“It’s just that they had no more funding from the government, so they couldn’t continue to work,” he told The Globe and Mail in an interview. “Canada could do more now − and they could have done more in the past.”
The 2014 report by Dr. Alimonti was obtained under the Access to Information Act by three researchers, including Prof. Herder.
He said he is concerned that Ottawa’s current emphasis on defence spending could reduce its support for health research, including scientific research on Ebola. The government should recognize that diseases such as Ebola are global security issues that could affect Canada, he said.
U.S. plan for Ebola quarantine in Kenya sparks anger
Adam Houston, a medical policy and advocacy adviser at MSF Canada, said the Ervebo trial is a reminder of Canada’s potential role in future vaccine development.
“It is really surprising that, despite the effectiveness of the original Ebola vaccine developed in the Government of Canada’s own laboratory, the Canadian government has been largely absent from efforts to further develop proven Canadian technology to tackle other viruses causing Ebola disease, including Bundibugyo,” he told The Globe.
The Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations is funding studies of four potential vaccines for Bundibugyo. One of them, developed by Moderna, is undergoing its first clinical trial at three sites in Canada.
Karine LeBlanc, a spokesperson for Health Canada, said the national lab in Winnipeg is continuing to conduct laboratory research on Ebola to develop vaccines, treatments and diagnostic tests, including possible Bundibugyo vaccines.
Preliminary data from an animal study at the lab, presented to the World Health Organization in July, demonstrated that Ervebo gave ferrets full protection from Bundibugyo, she noted.

title: Twenty years without Jorge Julio López, the man who disappeared twice
content:
In the early hours of September 18, 2006, Jorge Julio López, a humble 76-year-old retired builder, left his home in La Plata. He was on his way to court, where his lawyers were going to present their closing arguments against the man who had tortured and held him captive 30 years earlier, during the military dictatorship: Miguel Osvaldo Etchecolatz.
But López never arrived. His vanishment is classified as a forced disappearance, and his fate remains a mystery to this day.
López is considered the first and only person to have disappeared both during Argentina’s last military dictatorship, which lasted from 1976 to 1983, and again after democracy returned.
He was one of the main witnesses in the case against Etchecolatz, a former investigations director for the Buenos Aires Provincial Police and one of the dictatorship’s most feared repressors.
Etchecolatz was the first perpetrator to stand trial for crimes against humanity in 2006, following the annulment of the pardon laws issued in the late 1980s.
Three months before his disappearance, López testified about the ex-policeman’s heinous crimes. His testimony helped establish Etchecolatz’s role as a repressor. He was sentenced to life imprisonment the day after López went missing.
His second disappearance brought back phantoms from Argentina’s darkest period. While some — including authorities and his own family — initially thought the retired builder might have gotten lost or suffered a health issue, the main theory behind his absence is that Etchecolatz, members of the Buenos Aires Province Police or other groups opposed to the dictatorship trials — or all three — may have been behind it.
Those who support this thesis think López was kidnapped to send a message against the trials and force the judicial proceedings to be cancelled.
“We didn’t realize until much later that this had to do with his testimony,” his son, Rubén López, told the Herald ahead of the anniversary. “He didn’t just identify Etchecolatz but several other repressors.”
Twenty years on, the truth about what happened continues to be a mystery. No concrete evidence of his whereabouts has emerged, and the investigation remains open.
The first disappearance
Following the military coup d’état on March 24, 1976, López, then 46, began collaborating with Peronist guerrilla group Montoneros. He was kidnapped by the Buenos Aires Province Police on October 27 of that year, alongside several of his comrades.
Etchecolatz led the operation.
López spent time in four clandestine detention centers — known as “death camps” — in La Plata. He endured relentless torture with electric shocks and saw many of his jailmates and comrades shot in cold blood.
Decades later, López would testify in court about how Etchecolatz tortured him using the electric picana. “Turn it up a little more. This gringo was laughing before. Let’s kill this old son of a bitch,” the police chief would say, according to the victim’s account.
López was released after more than two years in captivity in June 1979.
Giving testimony
López began reuniting sporadically with his released jail mates after democracy was restored in 1983.
In 2006, after the pardon laws were abolished and the judiciary resumed the dictatorship trials, he joined a group of fellow survivors and human rights lawyers who were planning a legal strategy to prosecute the perpetrators.
“López wanted to be part of that process. He participated actively,” Guadalupe Godoy, one of the lawyers who represented him, told the Herald.
He gave a chilling testimony on June 28, 2006, visibly moved and affected by tremors that had begun several years earlier. He spoke about how Etchecolatz tortured him.
“My dad was anxious to testify. We understood why he was so insistent when we heard him speak. He had never told us anything,” his son Rubén López recalled.
“He let go of the weight he felt, the responsibility of speaking about what he had seen, about how his comrades were tortured and murdered,” Rubén said. For his father, speaking was “a moral duty,” but also a promise he had made to his cellmates.
López’s second disappearance
Monday, September 18, 2006, was the day the lawyers were due to present their closing arguments. López was not testifying that day, but he was required to be present so his lawyers, including Godoy, could speak on his behalf.
It was also a chance to come face to face with Etchecolatz, who had not been present when he testified. His son and lawyer said he wanted to see him again after all those years.
Rubén saw his father the night before. He was “calm, normal, although a little anxious,” he said.
That Monday morning Lopez’s younger son Gustavo, who lived at his parents’ house, got up early to prepare for his father’s hearing. López was nowhere to be found. The clothes he had worn to the previous hearings remained laid out on a chair.
The only things missing from the house were a small knife López used for gardening and a pair of boots he never used.
It became clear that something had happened when Gustavo arrived at the municipal building where the trial was being held and saw that his father was not there either. The lawyers had not seen him.
“At first, we thought he had suffered some kind of physical or mental episode, like a panic attack,” Rubén recalls.
However, fellow survivors and his lawyers interpreted the situation differently. “The only thing we knew is that his absence had something to do with the trial. At first we thought maybe he was distressed because he was remembering things, but we quickly realized it was something different,” Godoy says.
They felt certain López had been taken, just as he had been in 1976.
The family reported the disappearance at a police station, and the plaintiff did so at the federal court’s office handling the Etchecolatz case.
Rubén recalled that his father was not assigned custody or given any special protection after he testified. “We trusted the justice system and the state fully.”
“All Argentines believed that the repressors had finished doing their evil work in 1983, when democracy returned,” Rubén said. “After what happened to my dad, it became clear that they were still walking among us and carrying out the same practices from the dictatorship. We didn’t think this would happen to him again.”
What surprised many was that López’s second disappearance occurred during the government of Néstor Kirchner, who considered bringing justice to victims of the dictatorship a top priority.
“There was little preparation and foresight about the power still held by certain groups with links to the military dictatorship,” said journalist Miguel Graziano, author of the 2013 investigative book En el cielo nos vemos (See You In Heaven), based on the López case.
Graziano thinks there was a sense of naivety both within the state and among human rights organizations when it came to protecting witnesses. For national and provincial authorities, who initially denied that López may have been taken because of his testimony, the disappearance was “a hard blow,” Graziano added.
“Politically, for them it was better to deny it rather than accept it.”
A fruitless search
The investigation of his disappearance was plagued by irregularities and was described by Rubén as aimless. Despite the lawyers’ insistence, the authorities treated the absence as a missing-person case.
The Buenos Aires Province Police led the search, something human rights organizations opposed because of their suspicion that the force could be involved in the possible abduction.
Some witnesses said they had seen López walking around his neighborhood that morning. Investigators managed to follow his tracks for five blocks from his house to the door of Susana Gopar, a woman said to have worked as Etchecolatz’s secretary during the late 1970s. While she denied any links to the repressor, she appeared in Etchecolatz’s phone book.
Evidence of his tracks ended there, but her potential involvement was never proven.
In 2008, the judiciary began investigating the case as a “potential forced disappearance” and removed the Buenos Aires Province Police from the investigation at the request of human rights organizations.
“We wanted the investigation to center around those who wanted to stop the trials from continuing to maintain their impunity,” Godoy says.
In 2014, Etchecolatz was photographed holding a piece of paper with the name Jorge Julio López written on it during a judicial hearing in which he was convicted of human rights violations committed at a death camp. The incident was investigated, but the inquiry yielded no results.
The case today
Throughout the past two decades, endless false leads emerged. Investigators looked into millions of phone calls and the visitor registry for the prison where Etchecolatz and other repressors were held.
Some irregularities appeared in the registry, but overall, the investigations were inconclusive.
The Security Ministry currently offers a reward of AR$5 million (roughly US$3200) to anyone who contributes feasible information on the builder’s whereabouts.
“To me, this is a story of impunity because of sloppiness and bad decisions in the investigation,” Graziano said.
Despite the judiciary’s efforts, Rubén said, “the problem is that we don’t know anything.”
“There is very little evidence to prove who organized this and who carried it out. Someone planned this — we all think it might have been Etchecolatz or some of the other repressors,” Rubén said. “But someone else did the dirty work, because the repressors were all in jail at the time.”
Rubén summarized the situation with a bitter irony: “In 1977, almost six months after he disappeared, in the harshest moment of the dictatorship, my dad was able to let us know through another person that he was alive. Two months later, we were able to visit him,” he said.
“Today, 20 years after his second disappearance and in a democracy, when these things are not supposed to be happening, we still don’t know what happened to him,” the man lamented. “That sums up all the anger we feel: nobody protected him, and the case has not been resolved.”
The family is still demanding that López be found alive. They want to be told what happened to him and why he has not been found.
Godoy and Graziano believe that, despite the limited progress made over the past 20 years, the persistence of human rights groups will eventually help bring justice for López, even if it takes many more decades — as happened with Etchecolatz and in many other ongoing trials over crimes committed in the late 1970s.
Meanwhile, López is ever present in Rubén’s life. He decided to continue his father’s human rights activism, and also remembers him through daily, mundane activities that bring back memories from when he used to take him and Gustavo to work in his tool shed. “I use his shovel, his pick and his wheelbarrow every day.”
“I remember him by doing what he did, supporting his cause and other causes. Just trying to keep his legacy alive.”

title: Deputy Prime Minister wishes children a joyful, safe Mid-Autumn Festival
content:
HÀ NỘI — Deputy Prime Minister Phạm Thị Thanh Trà wished the children a joyful, safe and meaningful Mid-Autumn Festival, and encouraged them to stay healthy, behave well and study hard.
Trà made the request on Sunday afternoon during a visit by her delegation to Trung Môn Kindergarten’s Kim Phú campus in Minh Xuân Ward, the northern mountainous province of Tuyên Quang, where she presented gifts to teachers and children on the occasion of Mid-Autumn Festival.
She has called on the province to continue improving the learning environment, facilities, equipment and other essential conditions for educational institutions.
Teachers should devote their love, dedication and sense of responsibility to their pupils so that “every day at school is a happy day” and every lesson is genuinely useful and meaningful, she said.
This should be a key task for the province’s education sector in the 2026-27 academic year and the years ahead.
She also stressed that the Party and State always pay special attention to children and seek to create the best possible conditions for them to study, play, receive care and grow up surrounded by the love of their families, schools and society.
In recent years, child protection, care and education have received increasingly comprehensive attention, ranging from investment in facilities and improving teaching quality to creating safe and friendly educational environments, she said.
On the occasion, Trà and the delegation presented Mid-Autumn gifts to the children and a television to the kindergarten to help improve equipment for childcare, nurturing and education.
The delegation also presented 30 computer sets to six communes – Đồng Yên, Tiên Yên, Liên Hiệp, Nhữ Khê, Phú Lương and Trường Sinh – with five sets for each commune.
The equipment is expected to improve working conditions at grassroots level, enhance the local authorities’ capacity to apply information technology and meet requirements for handling work in the course of performing their duties.
Spreading love
Also on Sunday, the People’s Committee of the southern province of Tây Ninh organised a provincial-level Mid-Autumn Festival camp themed “A Loving Moon” for children in An Tịnh Ward, providing a space for fun, social interaction and meaningful experiences while demonstrating the care and attention given to children by authorities, sectors and society as a whole.
The camp brought together 10 teams and 100 children representing more than 10,801 children in An Tịnh Ward.
Amid the festive atmosphere of the eighth lunar month, the children took part in a range of fun and experiential activities, including decorating their camp areas, making lanterns and playing games such as “Keeping the Loving Moon”, “Bringing the Moon to the Team” and “Mid-Autumn Picture Puzzle”.
Cultural performances and lion dances also created a lively, warm and colourful atmosphere for the festival.
Nguyễn Hoàng Uyên, Deputy Director of the provincial Department of Health and head of the camp’s organising committee, said the event aimed to provide children with a joyful, healthy and useful playground while giving them opportunities to interact, gain experience and develop their sense of solidarity, creativity, confidence and individual talents.
The health sector considers childcare to go beyond ensuring physical health, nutrition and disease prevention, she said, stressing the need to pay attention to children’s mental health, living environment and comprehensive development.
In recent years, authorities, sectors and localities across the province have organised numerous activities to visit and present gifts to children and provide them with care, particularly those facing exceptionally difficult circumstances or at risk of falling into such circumstances.
These efforts have helped give children greater strength and encouragement to overcome difficulties and continue attending school, studying and developing themselves. — VNS

title: AI and robots drive administrative reform in Đồng Nai Province
content:
ĐỒNG NAI — The Đồng Xoài Ward Public Administrative Service Centre in Đồng Nai City has introduced a reception robot and a multichannel artificial intelligence system, including chatbots and voicebots, as part of efforts to accelerate administrative reform and build a digital government.
Capable of automatically welcoming visitors, recognising faces and providing spoken guidance and advice on administrative procedures, the new technology not only eases the workload of frontline officials but also improves the public’s experience.
Technology improves public services
People visiting the centre are now assisted by an intelligent reception robot.
Ngô Hoàng Lãng, a resident of Residential Area 2 in Đồng Xoài Ward, said he was surprised by the changes in administrative services when he visited the centre.
In the past, he often worried about complicated procedures and lengthy waiting times whenever he needed to complete paperwork. Since the ward stepped up its digital transformation and introduced AI and robots, administrative procedures have become simpler and more convenient.
The robot provides detailed guidance in a clear voice and directs visitors to the correct service counters. Meanwhile, the AI system available on mobile phones allows residents to access and look up information anytime and anywhere, without having to make repeated visits to the centre.
“Modern technology gives people access to more useful information about policies and application procedures in a transparent and clear manner,” Lãng said.
“These changes not only save time and effort but also make the service feel more accessible and welcoming. People are genuinely satisfied with and appreciative of the local administration’s commitment to serving them.”
Nguyễn Trọng Phát, a resident of Residential Area 1, also praised the convenience offered by the new technology.
He said administrative procedures were now much quicker and more convenient than before. What impressed him most was the detailed advice and guidance provided through AI applications.
In addition to explaining application procedures, the AI system answers questions and provides useful information about new policies and regulations that residents may not yet know about.
The introduction of AI and robots has enabled people to take a more active role in looking up information and completing administrative procedures, while creating a more open and transparent administrative environment. These technological services have helped residents feel more confident and satisfied when dealing with local authorities.
With its friendly appearance, the robot welcomes visitors, directs them to the appropriate specialist offices and gives spoken answers to common questions. Facial-recognition technology has also been integrated to meet modern management needs.
Residents who do not visit the centre in person can still check the status of their applications or quickly submit feedback through AI-powered chatbots and voicebots on the centre’s website and social media platforms.
Trần Anh Mỹ, Director of the Đồng Xoài Ward Public Administrative Service Centre, said the introduction of administrative guidance and reception robots, along with a multichannel AI system, marked a new step in the locality’s administrative reform efforts.
At the centre, the robots welcome visitors, provide guidance and answer questions about procedures and application status. AI tools, including chatbots and voicebots on the website and social media platforms, are available around the clock to help users look up information and submit feedback.
The technology not only reduces pressure on officials working at service counters but, more importantly, also improves service quality, he said.
It is also an important milestone demonstrating Đồng Xoài Ward’s determination to build a modern, transparent and people-friendly administration.
AI supports internal management
Đồng Xoài Ward is also expanding the use of artificial intelligence in its internal management.
In addition to an AI chatbot integrated into its online information portal to help residents quickly look up administrative procedures, the ward has incorporated tools such as Smart AI and a key performance indicator tracking system into its operations.
These tools enable officials and civil servants to use data, handle tasks and monitor progress more effectively.
Expanding AI from public services to internal management is a strategic step towards building a comprehensive digital government.
Nguyễn Thị Bích Thuần, Vice Chairwoman of the Đồng Xoài Ward People’s Council, said applying artificial intelligence to management was a key measure to improve the performance of the local administrative apparatus.
To achieve this goal, ward leaders have asked every official and civil servant to actively improve their digital skills and flexibly apply new technology to their professional duties. The ultimate aim is to build a modern and transparent administration dedicated to serving residents and businesses.
During the first nine months of 2026, the Đồng Xoài Ward Public Administrative Service Centre maintained the stable and lawful processing of administrative procedures.
From January 1 to September 15, the centre received more than 9,500 applications, all of which were submitted online.
It processed more than 9,300 applications, equivalent to over 98.5 per cent, while the remainder were still within the permitted processing period.
Notably, all completed applications were processed either on time or ahead of schedule, with none overdue.
These results lifted the ward’s public and business service index to 97.56 points, placing it ninth among Đồng Nai City’s 95 communes and wards.
The achievement also resulted from proactive communication and direct public support.
During the first nine months of the year, the centre helped organise 20 face-to-face guidance sessions in residential areas, attended by more than 9,000 people. It also provided information through multiple channels, including its website, public loudspeaker system and community Zalo groups.
Mỹ said the co-ordinated measures had reduced the number of applications requiring repeated additions and increased the proportion submitted online.
They have also gradually encouraged people to use digital public services, helping improve service quality and advance administrative reform in the locality.
To effectively implement Project 06 during the 2026–30 period and advance digital transformation, the centre will continue diversifying its communication activities and strengthening face-to-face guidance to help residents and businesses make effective use of digital technology.
It considers public satisfaction the key measure of its performance and will conduct regular monitoring and evaluations to maintain a 100 per cent satisfaction rate, while building an image of dedicated and professional officials and civil servants.
After more than five months, the use of AI and reception robots at the centre has proved to be a technological breakthrough that has improved the quality of public services.
By combining modern digital infrastructure, stronger internal governance and public support, Đồng Xoài Ward has demonstrated the practical effectiveness of its digital government model.
Its strong record of processing applications on time, together with high levels of public satisfaction, reflects progress towards a modern and transparent administration centred on the needs of residents and businesses. — VNS

title: Côte d’Ivoire-AIP/Des acteurs sociaux renforcent leurs capacités sur les droits à la santé sexuelle, reproductive et mentale à Doropo
content:
Doropo, 19 sept 2026 (AIP) – Des acteurs sociaux ont bénéficié d’un renforcement de capacités sur les droits à la santé sexuelle et reproductive (DSSR), la prévention de l’exploitation des abus sexuels (PSEA) et la santé mentale, lors d’un atelier régional organisé par l’ONG l’Etoile du Bounkani (EBONI), en partenariat avec Médecins du Monde (MdM), avec l’appui financier de l’Union Européenne (ECHO).
Cet atelier, organisé du 15 au 17 septembre 2026, à la préfecture de Doropo s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet « Réponse d’urgence pour l’accès aux soins de santé essentiels et renforcement des capacités de réponses aux chocs pour les populations affectées par la crise sahélienne dans le Nord-est de la Côte d’Ivoire »
Il vise à améliorer l’offre de services de santé et renforcer les mécanismes communautaires de résilience.
Lors de cette session de formation, les participants ont vu leurs compétences renforcées sur les droits à la santé sexuelle et reproductive (DSSR), la détection des signes d’alerte en matière de santé mentale, la conduite à tenir ainsi que leurs responsabilités dans la prise en charge des personnes présentant des risques de santé mentale.
La santé mentale repose sur les principes de dignité, de non-discrimination, de confidentialité, de consentement et de respect de la personne. L’atelier a également donné lieu à la gestion de cas pratiques de santé mentale, regroupant des leaders communautaires, guides religieux, travailleurs sociaux, les humanitaires et enseignants.
Selon les formateurs, les acteurs communautaires doivent être à l’écoute, dans le présent, respecter et adopter une attitude de non-jugement, éviter de projeter ses opinions, croyances et valeurs, savoir poser des questions et accepter ses limites, faire enfin preuve d’empathie.
Le directeur exécutif de l’ONG initiatrice de cet atelier, Dah Ollo Toussaint, a, pour sa part, rappelé que le contexte sécuritaire actuel de la région nécessitait d’accompagner les travailleurs sociaux et para-sociaux qui donnent chaque jour des soins, de leur temps dans l’accompagnement des populations impactées.
Ainsi, a-t-il invité les participants à prendre soin de leur santé mentale et à référer urgemment tout cas suspect pour une meilleure prise en charge.
(AIP)
