title: Noma: The neglected disease devastating children in northern Nigeria
content:
Nigeria
Ibrahim Dalhatu was just 3 years old when he contracted noma, a severe disease that disfigures the face and kills most of the children it infects.
He had his first facial reconstructive surgery in 2021 at the Noma Children Hospital in Nigeria's Sokoto state. Since then, Ibrahim, now 8, has had six operations to help him recover.
Noma is a rapidly progressing and often fatal infection of the face and mouth. It begins with gum inflammation in malnourished children living in polluted environments and quickly spreads to destroy soft tissues and bones. It mostly affects 2- to 6-year-old children, especially in poor communities.
Early-stage treatment includes antibiotics, wound care and improved nutrition. But once the disease worsens, surgery is required.
In Nigeria, health workers are seeing more noma patients. Doctors Without Borders, the humanitarian organization known by its French abbreviation MSF, is carrying out multi-stage operations free of charge as part of its efforts to tackle diseases.
Parents say the operations have given their children another chance to live a normal life, a relief for many in one of the world's poorest regions.
“I was very excited because I thought there was no solution to the disease,” said Muhammad Dalhatu, Ibrahim's father, an Islamic teacher married to a trader. “Before, I was worried about the cost of the treatment, but when I was told it was free of charge, I was so happy.”
A neglected disease rooted in poverty
Noma is classified by the World Health Organisation as a neglected tropical disease, meaning it receives little or no global attention and funding, despite its impact on victims. WHO has said evidence shows the disease “can be greatly reduced by early treatment.”
WHO has not updated its data on noma since 1998, when it estimated 140,000 cases per year with a 90% fatality rate. A study published in July in The Lancet Global Health journal, relying on data from the Sokoto hospital, reported over 50,000 noma cases across 12 northern Nigerian states between 1999 and 2024.
While it is hard to track how common the disease is in different countries, a so-called “noma belt” stretches across Africa, from Senegal and Mauritania in the west to Ethiopia in the east.
Yuka Makino, a technical officer for oral health at the agency’s Africa office, said research has shown that noma can be caused by 117 different microorganisms, calling it “an opportunistic, polymicrobial infection.”
But the major risk factors, experts say, are extreme poverty and severe malnutrition. WHO calls the disease “a marker of absolute poverty.” The United Nations Human Rights Council says the conditions leading to it constitute a human rights violation for affected children.
During the United Nations General Assembly, which begins Tuesday, WHO has said it will engage heads of state and partners to raise global awareness and advance shared solutions to diseases and other health challenges.
A worrisome trend takes hold in northern Nigeria
In northern Nigeria, ravaged by the fallout from armed violence and economic hardship, experts say more children are being diagnosed with noma. Many of those affected arrive late for treatment due to a lack of awareness and the deadly impact of the disease, MSF and medical officials said.
“We are seeing more acute noma cases, and we are veering toward awareness for the community so they can bring their children earlier to prevent tissue loss and require reconstructive surgery later in years,” said Bukola Oluyide, Nigeria medical coordinator at MSF.
According to WHO's Makino, Nigeria reports more noma cases than other countries due to its specialist hospitals, large population and a government-led response that likely ensures more cases are reported than in most other countries.
Neither the federal Ministry of Health nor the state ministry for Sokoto responded to a request for comment regarding the government's plans to combat the disease.
At the specialist hospital in Sokoto, more than 500 children with noma from across northern Nigeria were treated between 2023 and 2025, according to data seen by the AP. Others are waiting for surgery at the three sessions MSF runs each year for the children whose bodies can take it.
“It is quite worrisome,” said Dr. Abubakar Abdullahi Bello, the chief medical director of the Noma Children Hospital. “The disease damages the mouth tissues within a short period. It eats up the tissue within two weeks of onset if the patient does not receive treatment.”
Ibrahim has largely recovered. He can eat and speak normally after nasal fistula surgery, but not every child has the same opportunity. Nigeria has only two noma hospitals, including one in Abuja, recently built in 2023.
Maryam Sabiu's 4-year-old son, who was infected with noma in 2024, is one of those on the waiting list. The disease has created a hole in his left cheek, extending toward his left eye, but he is too young for surgery. He is in pain and cries constantly. His mother breastfeeds him frequently to soothe him. This has led to pain and stigmatisation, she said.
“I feel like the way people would stop and look at my child is one of the worst experiences in my entire life,” Sabiu said.

title: El Niño: Districts race to relocate families from high-risk areas
content: In Kibeho sector, Nyaruguru District, the new iron sheets on Alphonse Bizumuremyi's house are a painful reminder of the devastation caused by heavy rains. Bizumuremyi lost his wife, who was eight months pregnant, when rain-related disasters struck his home. He survived alongside his three-year-old child. ALSO READ: Govt steps up flood preparedness as strong El Niño looms “I lost both a house and a wife who was eight months pregnant. I survived with a three-year-old child,” he recalls. His house has since been rehabilitated, but the threat of further disasters remains. His neighbour, Faustin Niyomugabo, is reinforcing his house's foundation and ceiling as the country prepares for another potentially destructive rainy season. Residents are also digging erosion-control trenches and constructing drainage channels to divert runoff during heavy rains. Their efforts reflect a broader national push to protect vulnerable communities as Rwanda prepares for El Niño conditions, which are expected to bring above-normal rainfall to several parts of the country. According to the Ministry in charge of emergency management (MINEMA), 4,785 households have been relocated from high-risk areas across the country in 2026. ALSO READ: Parliament clears Rwf207bn for disaster response However, thousands of families remain exposed to flooding, landslides and other rain-related disasters, prompting districts to intensify relocation, drainage improvement and emergency preparedness measures. Where the heaviest rains are expected The Rwanda Meteorology Agency forecasts rainfall ranging from 300 to 1,000 millimetres during the season, compared with the usual range of 279mm to 962mm. Aimable Gahigi, the agency's Director General, said the forecast draws on weather patterns observed in 1997 and 2023, which resemble conditions expected in 2026. The highest rainfall, ranging from 800mm to 1,000mm, is expected in Nyamasheke, western Rutsiro and Karongi, western and southern Nyamagabe and Nyaruguru, and eastern Rusizi. Musanze, Gakenke, parts of Burera and Muhanga, and much of the Western Province are expected to receive between 600mm and 800mm. Gicumbi, Rulindo, Kigali, Huye, Nyanza, Ruhango and Nyagatare, alongside parts of Gisagara and Kamonyi, are forecast to receive between 450mm and 600mm. Gahigi warned that El Niño conditions could persist from October 2026 through January and February 2027. “January and February are a bit drier but they will be characterised by rains. We have to be well prepared,” he said. Thousands face relocation In the Western Province, Governor Jean Bosco Ntibitura said 2,799 households have been relocated from high-risk zones, while 17 evacuation sites have been identified across the province. Nyabihu District has identified 532 households requiring relocation and plans to provide rental support. Three evacuation sites have also been prepared. In Rusizi, Mayor Phanuel Sindayiheba said 400 households have already been relocated from high-risk areas, of which 317 will receive rental support. Surveillance teams have also been deployed to monitor areas classified as moderately at risk. Rubavu has identified 590 households requiring relocation and allocated Rwf201 million in its 2026/27 budget to construct houses for vulnerable families living in high-risk areas. Schools and other public facilities are being encouraged to install lightning protection systems. ALSO READ: Rwanda strengthens telecom systems for disaster response Karongi District has prepared two fully equipped evacuation sites, established disaster management command posts and trained response teams down to the cell level. In the Southern Province, Governor Alice Kayitesi said 2,268 households, mainly in Muhanga, Kamonyi and Nyamagabe, remain in high-risk areas and require relocation. Authorities have also identified roads, bridges, schools and other infrastructure vulnerable to flooding and landslides. “We are considering temporary relocation sites. Constructing drainage channels, clearing existing water drainage systems and maintaining erosion-control ditches are also key,” Kayitesi said. Muhanga District has identified 64 high-risk areas and 199 households requiring assistance to secure alternative accommodation. It has prepared 14 evacuation sites. Mayor Jacqueline Kayitare said the district is clearing drainage channels, maintaining erosion-control trenches and filling abandoned mining pits, while urging mining companies to strengthen worker safety. In Nyanza, 1,127 households have received support to secure their roofs, while 51 others received iron sheets to repair damaged roofing. The district has also cleared drainage channels and designated at least one evacuation site in every sector, with Kibirizi having two because of its terrain. Another 13 households in high-risk areas are being considered for relocation and rental support. Huye District Mayor Ange Sebutege said preparations include repairing damaged bridges, improving drainage infrastructure and working with the Red Cross to ensure emergency supplies are available. Northern districts step up preparedness Northern Province Governor Maurice Mugabowagahunde said 6,950 households were initially identified as living in high-risk zones across the province. Of these, 619 households were earmarked for immediate relocation, and 564 had been moved by June 2026. However, 6,386 households remain in high-risk areas, highlighting the scale of the relocation challenge facing the province. ALSO READ: Rwanda loses $300m to disasters annually - report Mugabowagahunde said authorities continue to provide temporary rental support to vulnerable families when heavy rainfall is expected, pending permanent relocation. Gakenke District has identified 49 disaster-prone hotspots and more than 881 households living in high-risk areas. Mayor Vestine Mukandayisenga said the district had requested rental assistance from MINEMA and begun relocating affected families. Community work in August focused on repairing damaged bridges and clearing drainage channels. Emergency evacuation sites, including Mugunga, have also been identified. In Musanze, 125 residents identified in high-risk areas have been relocated, according to Theobard Kayiranga, the district's Vice Mayor in Charge of Social Affairs. The district has trained disaster-response teams comprising youth volunteers, security personnel, para-social workers and Red Cross volunteers. At the national level, MINEMA said 14 emergency evacuation sites have been established in four districts: Kigali, Musanze, Kayonza and Karongi. Emergency relief warehouses have also been established to support disaster response. Across the country, authorities are combining relocation, infrastructure repairs, drainage maintenance and emergency response preparations to reduce the potential impact of the coming rains. For families such as Bizumuremyi's, who have already experienced the devastating consequences of extreme weather, those preparations could mean the difference between safety and another tragedy.

title: Akdital acquires majority stake in Mecca hospital, launches Saudi operations
content: According to a statement obtained by Le360, the facility will now operate under its new brand and corporate identity, Akdital Mecca.“This deal marks a major milestone in the group’s regional expansion in Saudi Arabia and reflects its firm commitment to contributing to the sustainable development of the country’s healthcare system, in line with the ambitious economic and development goals of Saudi Vision 2030,” the statement said.Commenting on the acquisition, Dr. Rochdi Taleb, CEO of Akdital, said the deal represents the successful transition from strategic planning to implementation.Akdital enters Saudi market with first hospital in Riyadh“Completing this acquisition marks a successful transition from strategic planning to implementation on the ground. Akdital Mecca is expected to play a central role in our expansion strategy in the Kingdom,” he said.“Our vision is to turn the facility into a leading medical center that combines clinical excellence, the highest patient safety standards and high-quality services, while fully integrating with the local healthcare system. The scale of the planned investment clearly reflects our long-term vision and our determination to play a key role in strengthening and developing healthcare services in Saudi Arabia,” he added.Comprehensive investment program launched to upgrade and expand hospitalFollowing the acquisition, Akdital has launched a major investment program to overhaul the hospital’s infrastructure and increase its bed capacity.According to the statement, the hospital’s total capacity is expected to rise to 126 beds once the development work is completed, up from 120 currently. The investment program also includes a comprehensive upgrade of its medical and technical infrastructure, a redesign of patient-care pathways to improve operational efficiency, and expanded capabilities in emergency care, intensive care, cardiology, surgery, and maternal and child health.Fez-Meknes brings hospitals, health centers under single regional managementThe planned facilities and capacity include 19 specialized emergency care units, including two clinical resuscitation units; 18 multidisciplinary resuscitation beds; eight cardiac intensive care beds; seven neonatal resuscitation beds, including one isolation bed; 13 nursery beds; seven advanced main operating rooms; one dedicated obstetrics operating room; one endoscopy room; and four delivery rooms.The hospital will also have an integrated medical imaging platform and a specialized medical laboratory.As a multispecialty hospital, Akdital Mecca will provide advanced healthcare services in areas including cardiology, interventional cardiology, general surgery, intensive care and resuscitation, obstetrics and gynecology, neonatology, emergency medicine and medical imaging.Dr. Shadi El Masri, Akdital’s medical director in Saudi Arabia, said the healthcare market in Mecca has unique needs, with the city having to serve both its growing resident population and the increasing number of pilgrims visiting throughout the year.“Saudi Arabia welcomed more than 18 million Umrah pilgrims and international Hajj pilgrims in 2025, and aims to increase its capacity to 30 million visitors a year by 2030,” he said.“In this context, Akdital Mecca will bring real added value to the holy city by offering a broad range of medical specialties, increased capacity in emergency and critical care, as well as rigorous medical governance designed to ensure operational flexibility during peak periods and periods of high patient flows,” he added.Through the strategic acquisition, Akdital plans to draw on its healthcare expertise to serve Mecca residents and pilgrims while contributing to higher quality standards, modernizing medical infrastructure, transferring knowledge and developing local skills.New 33-story university hospital nears completion in Morocco’s capitalAkdital develops and operates a broad network of multispecialty and specialized healthcare facilities. The group currently has a capacity of 4,864 beds across 45 healthcare facilities in 26 cities throughout Morocco.Its workforce currently stands at 10,256 employees across its facilities, including 362 people recruited since the beginning of 2026.Following its successful listing on the Casablanca Stock Exchange in December 2022 under the ticker AKT, Akdital continues to pursue its expansion strategy, with plans to grow its network and strengthen its position in the healthcare sector.

À Molenbaix, l’art contemporain s’invite dans les rues et les champs et attire des visiteurs de toute la Wallonie
content:
À Molenbaix, l'art contemporain s'invite dans les rues et les champs et attire des visiteurs de toute la Wallonie
Il reste deux semaines pour découvrir "Butor", la première biennale d'art contemporain en campagne. Dix-neuf artistes, entre champs et hameaux.
- Publié le 19-09-2026 à 12h01
Le centre du village et le hameau de Butor voient passer de nombreux visiteurs, depuis quelques semaines. Ils viennent de différents coins de Wallonie, mais aussi des Flandres et de France.
"Butor" et douceur
Marcher de la ferme d'Ecavée au centre du village permet de découvrir un sentier singulier, en céramique gravée de mots. "De Molenbeek à Molenbaix", "Ce chemin est celui de tous" ... Citadins et ruraux se souviennent de venelles, sentes, petites voies, ruelles, chemins de pavés et de liens. Les enfants apprécient particulièrement cette oeuvre de Various Artists, un collectif également auteur d'un totem et de quelques interventions insolites.
"C'est ma petite-fille !" annonce fièrement Christian Collie quand des visiteurs s'approchent du terrain de foot. Léa - en miroir - est peinte par Charlotte Beaudry sur bois chantourné, aux couleurs du club. La jeune footballeuse de quinze ans joue à présent à Avelgem, elle est de plus, vu son talent, reprise dans la sélection nationale des Jeunes à Mons. Son grand-père, qui évolua au Racing de Tournai, fait partie du comité de foot de Molenbaix.
Un pas plus loin, Raphaël De Coster a créé une "zone de rupture potentielle", en utilisant un cordeau. Ligne droites et penchées, tendues vers la cime d'une structure qui puise son énergie dans un geste géométrique résolu. Chemin du centre, Lise Duclaux a placé des affiches porteuses de slogans courts, limpides : "Nous ne sommes que les autres". L'église Saint-Ghislain abrite des recherches picturales de Charlotte Beaudry, un autel à sainte Rita (Jacques Charlier) et une étonnante sculpture de Maaerten Vanden Eynde : un tronc d'arbre scié, posé sur une ancienne balance en fonte. L'oeuvre interroge l'équilibre, la fragilité, la pesanteur.
Lieux et liens
"C'est un choc, ce jaillissement !", s'exclame Frédérique, venue de Lasne à la rencontre de l'exposition. Devant "La terre saigne", fontaine de Laurence Dervaux, elle évoque son réflexe de "juguler la plaie", "voir arriver une ambulance" "une énorme puissance suggestive" . "Des visiteurs parlent ici autant de vie que de mort, songeant aux guerres comme aux souffrances infligées à la planète", souligne Caroline, l'une des guides de l'exposition.
Des groupes et duos se croisent, échangeant leurs impressions à propos du parcours, de la campagne, des nombreuses haltes proposées. Aucun artiste n'est oublié dans les conversations, les précisions et questions. Les interventions en extérieur comme en intérieur ouvrent des perspectives, déclenchent la surprise, l'admiration, la réflexion collective. Et cette certitude d'être au coeur d'une approche que l'on dit contemporaine : l'intégration au paysage, à la nature, l'assurance d'une discrétion privilégiée, la présence du symbole et de la beauté.
"Butor", au départ de la ferme d'Ecavée à Molenbaix, du jeudi au dimanche, de 10h30 à 18h. Possibilité de visites guidées. Jusqu'au 4 octobre.

title: Birdwatching boom connects youth with natural world
content:
Birdwatching boom brings young people to Australia's 'shorebird capital'
The unabated boom in birdwatching is welcome news to one of Australia's most remote bird sanctuaries near Broome in Western Australia's Kimberley.
Broome Bird Observatory warden Jamie Van Jones said the increased interest from young people was "fantastic".
"I'm getting lots of passionate young people through the observatory, lots of young people on tour with a list of birds they want to see," she said.
"If you talk stereotypes around birdwatchers, it's khaki clothes, binoculars and cameras, a bum bag — a dorky look. That's changed."
There are different categories of birdwatchers, with "twitchers" or "listers" renowned for dropping everything to catch a glimpse of a rare bird or spot as many types as possible.
Ms Van Jones said birdwatchers were enthusiasts of any age who travelled widely to find new birds and experience nature.
She has been a wildlife guide around the world for a decade and spent the past two years at the Broome Bird Observatory.
The charitable organisation is dedicated to research and education on shorebirds, such as godwits and knots, which migrate between Roebuck Bay and the Northern Hemisphere.
"People are craving to be outside. It's about being connected to the outdoor world, and when you're birding, you're in the moment," Ms Van Jones said.
Young birders connect with nature
The increase in young Aussies birdwatching is attributed to pandemic lockdowns forcing people to slow down and take up "nana technology" hobbies like knitting, crochet or baking bread.
When Ella Kerr scrolls through her phone, she is looking at lists of birds she has seen or checking their identity on an app.
The 29-year-old Melbourne woman caught the birdwatching bug during long COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns in 2020 and 2021.
"There were just all these birds … I was seeing parts of our environment I hadn't noticed until then," Ms Kerr said.
Ms Kerr planned her holiday to Darwin and Broome around birdwatching and was keen to tick some birds unique to northern Australia off her list.
"I like that it gets me out into nature, just listening to the sounds," she said.
"And when you see a new bird, it's even more exciting."
It is a sentiment shared by 21-year-old Will Vasic, who travelled from Melbourne to work at the Broome Bird Observatory.
"I never really thought I'd get into it at such a young age," he said.
"But it's got me places where I never thought I'd go."
Social media driving birder trend
Birdwatching has been dubbed a "new form of meditation" in Hollywood, as celebrities embrace the pastime and podcast about it.
Young birdwatchers are enthusiastically posting their sights on social media.
Callum Wells formed the Talbot Bay Birdwatching Club (TBBC) in the remote Kimberley last year with friends.
"We're trying to break down that stigma from it being a bit nerdy to getting out there looking for birds is something that everyone should appreciate," he said.
TBBC has become a social media sensation because of its larrikin humour.
Followers share their own birding finds with Mr Wells, including British actor Sean Bean, who hosts the Get Birding podcast.
"When Boromir from Lord of the Rings [Sean Bean] is commenting on your stuff, you're pretty excited!"Mr Wells said.
Mr Wells said while birdwatching had taken him to "amazing places", it allowed him to spend time with mates and have a laugh.
"It's good, clean fun," the 33-year-old said.
Ms Van Jones hoped birdwatching encouraged people to be more environmentally aware.
"There are so many threats to the natural world and, through connection, they start to care and be the future champions for the environment," she said.

title: El ecoturismo y la ‘economía emocional’ han logrado la conservación de la Sierra Gorda de Querétaro
content:
Para quienes gustan de manejar en carretera y pueblear, hay una ruta peculiar que incluye diversos atractivos. Comienza en el Pueblo Mágico de Peña de Bernal, en Querétaro, y luego se enfila hacia la Sierra Gorda, donde se encuentran las Misiones que fundó Fray Junípero Serra en el siglo XVIII: de Santiago de Jalpan, de Nuestra Señora de la Luz de Tancoyol, de Santa María del Agua de Landa, de San Francisco de Asís del Valle de Tilaco y la de San Miguel Concá, todas con inverosímiles fachadas por las que en 2003 fueron declaradas Patrimonio Mundial por la UNESCO. De ahí, al punto final cruzando hacia el estado de San Luis Potosí, Xilitla, que también es Pueblo Mágico y alberga la casa surrealista que construyó Sir Edward James, conocida como Las Pozas.
Todos esos puntos de la ruta son espectaculares, pero lo mejor de todo es que buena parte del trayecto se realiza cruzando la Sierra Gorda de Querétaro, que ofrece su propio espectáculo, el de la naturaleza, donde habitan más de cien mil personas distribuidas en 638 comunidades dispersas en 383 mil 567 hectáreas de Área Natural Protegida, declarada como tal por el presidente Ernesto Zedillo en 1997.
Actualmente, en este lugar funciona una red de alrededor de 65 microempresas comunitarias de Ecoturismo, en las cuales trabajan trescientas familias y grupos comunitarios que ofrecen diversos servicios a los visitantes, desde caminatas guiadas y experiencias culturales, hasta alojamiento en cabañas de barro, comida –cuentan con 26 fondas-- y espacios para acampar, además de talleres artesanales como elaboración de quesos, bordados y herbolaria, entre otros, con lo que ponen en valor lo que la naturaleza les dio: una gran biodiversidad y la belleza escénica del paisaje, recursos que llegan directamente a los negocios locales, haciendo de la conservación del sitio una actividad lucrativa.
Pero esto no surgió de manera espontánea, tiene su historia, ya larga, cuando Pati Ruiz Orozco, maestra de música en una secundaria de la ciudad de Querétaro, se mudó con su familia a una comunidad en las montañas de la Sierra Gorda, para en 1987 fundar junto con habitantes locales el Grupo Ecológico de la Sierra Gorda (GESG), con el objetivo de crear conciencia sobre la biodiversidad, sus amenazas y un movimiento de base para construir un futuro regenerativo en la región. Diez años después, lograrían que se les decretara como Área Natural Protegida y Zedillo la nombró directora federal de la Reserva de Biosfera Sierra Gorda, cargo que desempeñó hasta 2009. Entonces regresó a dirigir el GESG.
Pati –como gusta que le digan-- desarrolló lo que denomina “economía emocional” y que define como un “conjunto de valores, emociones, conocimientos, capacidades y sentimientos que permiten que una comunidad se involucre en la conservación y mantenga en el tiempo las soluciones que hacen posible regenerar la naturaleza”.
Pero los retos han sido muchos, por ejemplo, la basura. Pati Explica que en una zona montañosa, con pequeñas comunidades distantes unas de otras, recolectar y transportar basura representa un enorme reto logístico. Para enfrentar este problema que durante décadas contaminó los cuerpos de agua y degradó el suelo, han construido, apoyado y equipado más de 170 centros de acopio comunitarios, en los que cada año recolectan nueve mil toneladas de materiales reciclables como vidrio, plástico, cartón, Tetra Pack y hasta chatarra de carros, que cada uno vende en Querétaro y en cuya comercialización no interviene el GESG.
Catalogada como una Institución de Asistencia Privada, el GESG es una Organización no Gubernamental que se sustenta en donaciones de particulares, fundaciones, organismos internacionales y fondos públicos como los de Sello Querétaro, un programa del gobierno estatal que implica un impuesto de carbono para las empresas más contaminantes. Las comunidades pusieron 50 mil hectáreas en modo de regeneración natural y a cambio reciben recursos de este programa.
Pati se emociona, y con razón, al hablar de todo lo que hecho durante ya casi cuatro décadas, labor que le ha merecido cincuenta premios internacionales y el reconocimiento de las comunidades.

title: Unions demand paternity leave for Namibian fathers
content:
Workers’ unions are calling on the government to consider introducing paternity leave to allow both parents to care for newborn babies.
The call follows justice and labour relations minister Wise Immanuel’s announcement yesterday of an increase in Social Security Commission (SSC) benefits such as maternity and sick leave, disability, retirement and death fund, effective 1 October.
The minister announced that maternity benefits will increase from N$15 000 to N$20 000 as from 1 October, while sick leave benefits will rise from N$11 250 to N$15 000 for the first 12 months and from N$9 750 to N$13 000 for the final 12 months.
Death, retirement and disability benefits will each increase from N$12 000 to N$15 000.
Affirmative Repositioning parliamentarian Frederick Shitana says the minister had done well, but adds that men remain excluded from benefiting.
In response, the minister reiterated in the National Assembly yesterday that Namibia has no statutory paternity leave provision, adding that employers offering it do it at their discretion.
He said institutions may, however, introduce paternity leave through their respective employment or industrial policies.
“Institutions that may have paternity leave are doing it on their own and it is not prohibited in any way. They are allowed,” he said yesterday.
National Union of Namibian Workers (NUNW) secretary general Job Muniaro yesterday said men are equal parents and should be given an opportunity to support their partners and bond with their newborn babies during the early stages of parenthood.
He said women should not be left to bear the responsibilities and consequences of childbirth alone.
“Children grow healthier in the care of both parents. The mother cannot experience pregnancy and even after pregnancy alone. They need to recover,” he said.
However, he welcomed the increase, saying it would help parents meet the costs of caring for their babies, especially those earning less than N$20 000.
“The increment is long overdue, considering the cost of living and the cost of caring for a baby. It will cover 50 to 70% of workers earning below N$20 000,” he said.
Mineworkers Union of Namibia (MUN) secretary general George Ampweya yesterday said the union supports the implementation of paternity leave, describing it as a social issue.
He said men need to be present in the lives of their newborn babies.
“We are in support of benefits that support men,” he said.
“These social things we’re experiencing now may be a result of absent fathers. We are happy about the increase, although it is not absolute, it is a step in the right direction,” Ampweya said.
The union had previously made a submission to NUNW for the labour minister to introduce paternity leave.
“The current setup sort of excludes fathers from the critical years of their children. We want fathers to be able to bond and support their partners during that time,” Ampweya said.
SSC contributions are monthly payments shared equally between employers and employees to fund the maternity, sick leave and death fund.
Employees earning a basic salary of N$500, according to SSC acting chief executive Ben Nangombe, contribute N$4 per month, while those earning between N$501 and N$12 000 contribute 0.9% of their basic salary.
The Cabinet in 2023 approved the introduction of paternity leave to the Labour Act and directed that it be adopted in the public service.
It also directed the labour ministry and the Employment Creation and relevant role-players, through the tripartite taskforce, to review the Labour Act to broaden the scope of compassionate leave to cover paternity leave and the extension of the period of unpaid maternity leave from 12 to 14 weeks.

title: Have an Apple iPhone 15 or 16? How to file a claim for up to $95.
content:
Apple settlement offers eligible iPhone owners up to $95. Here is how to file a claim.
The claim window is now open for an Apple settlement announced earlier this year, giving certain iPhone users the chance to get up to $95.
Apple agreed to pay $250 million to settle claims that it misled customers about Siri's Apple Intelligence features. Customers who were part of the class action lawsuit said they purchased iPhones expecting certain Siri features they allegedly did not receive.
"The $250 million settlement fund represents the largest false advertising settlement in history," Ryan Clarkson, co-lead counsel on the class-action lawsuit and founder and managing partner of Clarkson Law Firm, said in an email to CBS News.
Apple declined to comment. The company has previously denied the allegations. According to the settlement agreement, the settlement shall "not be construed in any fashion as an admission of liability or wrongdoing by Apple."
Here's what to know about eligibility and how to file a claim.
How do I file a claim?
iPhone users can visit SmartphoneAISettlement.com to file a claim, according to a spokesperson for Clarkson Law Firm, a public interest law firm.
The person must input basic personal information, including their name, address and phone number. They must also enter their iPhone's serial number, which can be found in the phone's Settings section.
Once they finish inputting that information, they can select the payment method. The options are PayPal, Venmo, direct deposit or check.
As SmartphoneAISettlement.com points out, consumers are limited to "one cash payment per eligible device." If they purchased another iPhone that meets the eligibility requirements, they must complete a separate claim form.
How do I know if I am eligible?
If you bought an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, or any iPhone 16 model between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, you're eligible to file a claim.
According to SmartphoneAISettlement.com, the person filing a claim must be the person who originally purchased the device. The phone must also be for personal or professional use, not for resale.
If you're not sure if you're eligible, you can call 1-888-988-8945 or write to this address for information: Landsheft, et al. v. Apple Inc.; Settlement Administrator; P.O. Box 301132; Los Angeles, CA 90030-1132.
How long do I have to file a claim?
The claims window is open until Dec. 21, 2026.
How much money will I receive?
Customers who submit a valid claim form will initially get $25 per eligible device. However, that amount may be increased up to $95 or decreased depending on the "total number of valid claims submitted and other factors," the claims website says.
When will I get the payment?
A district court in San Jose, California, will hold a hearing on Feb. 24, 2027, to decide whether to approve the settlement. If there are any appeals, it could delay the payment process.
"If there is no appeal, your settlement benefit will be processed promptly," according to the claim website.

title: Mokiniai dalyvaus sporto ir meno šventėje „Adamkiada“, skirtoje Valdo Adamkaus 100-mečiui
content:
Vytauto Didžiojo universiteto (VDU) prezidento Valdo Adamkaus sporto centre šeštadienį vyks vienuoliktoji respublikinė sporto ir meno šventė „Adamkiada“, kurioje dalyvaus moksleivių komandos iš 25 Lietuvos mokyklų.
Šiųmetė „Adamkiada“ skiriama artėjančiam prezidento Valdo Adamkaus 100-ajam jubiliejui. Planuojama, kad jis dalyvaus renginio atidaryme ir pasakys sveikinimo kalbą.
Organizatorių teigimu, prezidento asmeninis dėmesys jaunimui ir aktyviam gyvenimo būdui kiekvienais metais suteikia renginiui ypatingą dvasią, įkvėpdamas moksleivius siekti aukštumų tiek moksle, tiek sporte ar mene.
Šventės metu moksleiviai varžysis sporto rungtyse mišriose komandose, dalyvaus dailės plenere „Laiškas Prezidentui“ ir dainų festivalyje „Šimtmečio karta: dainuojame Lietuvai“, išbandys jėgas pramoginėse atrakcijose bei loterijoje.
Renginyje taip pat pasirodys Alytaus muzikos mokyklos simfoninis orkestras „Svajonė“ ir atlikėjas Linas Adomaitis.
„Adamkiados“ organizatorių teigimu, renginys tęsia tradiciją, kurią anksčiau puoselėjo Almos Adamkienės labdaros ir paramos fondas. Jis ilgus metus rėmė mokinius, mokytojus ir švietimo įstaigas iš Lietuvos regionų.
Organizatoriai teigia, kad šventės tikslas – suburti skirtingų Lietuvos regionų moksleivius, sudaryti jiems galimybę varžytis sporto ir meno rungtyse bei susipažinti su bendraamžiais.
„Adamkiadą“ organizuoja Alytaus rajono Butrimonių gimnazija ir VDU.
